summary: Palmira Brummett is a historian and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Chicago (1975) and an MPH from the University of Illinois (1981). She held posts at the University of Tennessee (c. 1987–2011) and Brown University (2011–2016).
Palmo Kyi is a Tibetologist who studied under Per Kværne, Hanna Havnevik, and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She was affiliated with Temple University in 2001 and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna and conducted research at the Australian National University from circa 1972 to 1976.

Pandurang Vaman Kane was an Indologist who studied at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He taught at Elphinstone High School, Elphinstone College, Wilson College, and Government Law College, later serving as vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).

Paolo Visigalli works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, having studied at the Sapienza University of Rome, University of Padua, and University of Cambridge. He has held positions at New York University Shanghai and Shanghai Normal University (attested 2025).

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied as a doctoral student at the University of Chicago and held a postdoctoral researcher post at Ghent University (both attested 2026).

Parimal G. Patil is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University (c. 1991–1993) and the University of Chicago (c. 1993–2002). Around 2004, he became a Professor at Harvard University.

Parul Dave-Mukherji is an Indologist and art historian who completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991). She has served as a professor of Visual Studies and Art History at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pascale Haag is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle University and under Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre University. She held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences around 2003.
Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania. She has served as a professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).
Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He has held posts at the University of Bristol and the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, where she became Professor Emerita. She also worked at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco and the Numata Center.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University. She held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).

Patricia Fister is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Kansas. She held positions at the Spencer Museum of Art, University of Kansas, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

Patricia Schiaffini-Vedani is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. She pursued graduate studies at Peking University (1990–1994) and earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of Perry Link.

Patrick Arthur Pranke is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (attested 2004) under the supervision of Luis O. Gómez and Victor Lieberman.

Patrick McAllister is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna (c. 2005–2011). Around 2011, he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences and its Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Patrick Olivelle is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford and earned his Ph.D. under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Indiana University Bloomington (1974–1991) and the University of Texas at Austin.
